page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-16-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the z4d server family. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The system is equipped with 126.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory allocation of approximately 7.88 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes 7516 GB of NVMe SSD capacity distributed across two local drives. No graphics processing units are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a resource density perspective, this virtual machine offers a high ratio of local NVMe SSD storage relative to its compute and memory resources. The inclusion of 7516 GB of local storage provides significant local read and write capacity directly attached to the instance, which reduces reliance on network-attached storage. However, because the storage is local NVMe SSD, data persistence is tied to the lifecycle of the instance, representing a key operational tradeoff. The hardware profile is structured for workloads requiring high-capacity local scratch space or caching layers without the overhead of external storage arrays.

The hardware configuration of this instance makes it suitable for storage-intensive and database workloads. Specifically, the combination of 126.0 GB of RAM and 7516 GB of local NVMe SSD storage aligns with the requirements of relational databases, NoSQL databases, high-throughput transactional systems, and data analytics pipelines that require fast local disk access. It is also applicable for distributed file systems and caching nodes where high-capacity local storage and moderate memory density are required.
